Title: MCP Search Tools Current State
Content: MemorySmith.App exposes POST /api/memories/search for lexical ranking, POST /api/memories/search/semantic for semantic ranking, POST /api/memories/search/hybrid for lexical plus semantic Reciprocal Rank Fusion, and /mcp for HTTP JSON-RPC tool access. Search input is plain text plus explicit filters, not a Lucene query-parser language: query text is tokenized and scored across title, tags, references, and content; tags are comma-separated exact-match filters with any-match semantics; status accepts Unconsolidated, Working, Core, or Deprecated; and namespaced tags such as kind:rule, audience:agent, and scope:configuration are matched literally. Field targeting, boolean, wildcard, fuzzy, and date-range syntax are not part of the supported public contract. Semantic ranking uses optional ONNX embeddings when configured and available, with local token, tag, title, reference, and alias scoring as fallback. The HTTP MCP search tools are memorysmith_search, memorysmith_semantic_search, memorysmith_hybrid_search, memorysmith_context_pack, memorysmith_get, memorysmith_page_search, memorysmith_page_get, memorysmith_unified_search, memorysmith_source_bundle, and memorysmith_find_by_source. memorysmith_search keeps its compatible tool name but returns lexical results rather than the old simple substring path. memorysmith_search, memorysmith_semantic_search, memorysmith_hybrid_search, and memorysmith_unified_search support markdown by default and structured output through format=json or format=envelope; the current parser also accepts json-v2 as a compatibility alias, but public MCP docs should use the advertised markdown, json, and envelope values. memorysmith_context_pack supports markdown or json and returns memorysmith.context-pack.v1 in structured mode. memorysmith_page_search and memorysmith_page_get are markdown-only today. REST memory search endpoints expose structured retrieval through format=envelope or format=json-v2, and REST page list or search exposes structured results through format=json, format=envelope, or format=json-v2. Structured memory-search envelopes use memorysmith.retrieval-results.v1 with schemaVersion, mode, provider, results, and warnings; hybrid Score is an RRF ranking value, not confidence. For larger KB workflows, prefer memorysmith_context_pack when an agent needs search results plus linked reference or conflict context in one response, then use memorysmith_source_bundle only for the narrowed evidence set. MCP memory and page tools require normal view access, page tools filter by each page minimum visibility role, page save or delete requires edit permission, and source_bundle or find_by_source are SensitiveRead MCP-only tools gated by CanReadSourceBundle because they can resolve local source-link file slices. .vscode/mcp.json points directly at http://localhost:5089/mcp. The /chat agent now uses ChatToolCatalog and an app-intercepted MCP-compatible read-only loop for memorysmith_unified_search, memorysmith_search, memorysmith_semantic_search, memorysmith_hybrid_search, memorysmith_context_pack, memorysmith_get, memorysmith_page_search, and memorysmith_page_get. It accepts model output shaped as toolCalls JSON or JSON-RPC tools/call, executes tools locally, and feeds results back into the same turn. ChatIntentInterceptor also handles clearly worded wiki intents before provider generation, for example page get, context pack, and unified search. Source bundle and find_by_source remain HTTP MCP tools for external agents and are not chat-side model-requested tools. The implementation is covered by McpAndSemanticSearchTests, ChatToolCatalogAndInterceptTests, MemoryApplicationServiceTests, and PagesAndChatTests, which use copied Data/Memories fixtures so the source project wiki remains stable.
